briefs.description: R1: a question about the canvas is answered from gh_get_all; nothing is written and nothing is reviewed.
briefs.userPrompt: What's on my canvas right now?

briefs.description: R2: "add a slider" with no brief must not write; the product expects the model to pause with ask_user.
A complete parametric brief: a circle whose radius is driven by a slider; decomposition, discovery, two adds and a wire.
briefs.userPrompt: Create a circle on the XY plane at the origin whose radius is driven by a number slider. Inputs: the radius, from 1 to 10 m (my numbers). Rule: the circle is always centred on the origin. Principle: a one-parameter column footprint. Evaluation: keep the footprint area at or below 50 m2; I will judge it by reading the area. Go ahead and build it.

briefs.description: R3: the rainscreen brief (depth and stagger inputs, thermal-break rule, minimise solar gain); decomposition and the input sliders.
briefs.userPrompt: Set up the inputs for a staggered rainscreen facade. Inputs: panel course depth 0.1 to 0.4 m and horizontal stagger 0 to 0.5 of a panel width (both mine). Rule: the thermal break behind the panels must stay continuous. Principle: alternate course depths to break up the facade. Evaluation: minimise solar gain on the south facade, which I will check with an annual radiation study. Start by adding the depth and stagger sliders.

briefs.description: Attractor grid: grid of points, circles whose radius shrinks with distance to an attractor; needs discovery of several components.
briefs.userPrompt: Build an attractor grid: a rectangular grid of points (5 to 20 points per side, spacing 1 to 3 m) and a circle at every point whose radius shrinks with the distance to an attractor point. Inputs: grid count, spacing, attractor x and y. Rule: radius = distance remapped into 0.1 to 0.5 m. Principle: an attractor-driven perforation pattern. Evaluation: keep every radius at least 0.1 m. Build it.

briefs.description: R5: the user locked the radius slider; a request to change it must leave the canvas unchanged and say it is locked.
A plugin that is not installed (Weaverbird): the model checks the loaded libraries and says so instead of inventing components.
briefs.userPrompt: Use Weaverbird's Catmull-Clark subdivision to smooth a 10 x 10 x 4 m box mesh, two levels.

briefs.description: A full brief that needs a component the model must look up (Voronoi): gh_find_component, then adds by the returned componentGuid.
briefs.userPrompt: Make a 2D Voronoi paving pattern: 30 random points inside a 20 x 20 m rectangle, with the Voronoi cells clipped to it. Inputs: point count 10 to 50 and a random seed (mine). Rule: cells stay inside the rectangle. Principle: a random cellular partition for paving. Evaluation: keep the cell count equal to the point count. Build it.

briefs.description: A small edit on an existing canvas (wire the slider into the circle); the gate still needs a recorded decomposition first.
briefs.userPrompt: Connect the radius slider to the circle's radius input.

briefs.description: A conceptual question needs no tools and no writes.
briefs.userPrompt: What does the Graph Mapper component do, and when would I use it?

transcript.content: What does the Graph Mapper component do, and when would I use it?

The **Graph Mapper** component lets you transform a numeric input (or a list of numbers) into a new value using a user‑defined curve.  
- **Input**: a number (or list) and a graph (curve).  
- **Output**: the corresponding value on the graph at the input’s x‑coordinate (or the y‑value of the graph at that x).  

Use it when you want to remap or “warp” a set of values according to a custom mapping curve—e.g., to create non‑linear scaling, apply easing functions, or shape a distribution of parameters in a parametric model. It’s handy for tuning gradients, controlling density, or generating smooth transitions that aren’t achievable with simple linear scaling.
